subject: How to code two different residual errors in Stan

messages.author: ac6f95129862ba28
messages.subject: How to code two different residual errors in Stan
parts:
Dear all,

I have a model looks like below (only part of the code shown).
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
model {   .....

   ipred[j] = (1-flag_g)*(function_1) + flag_g*(function_2);

if (flag_g == 0) { sigma = sigma_m;}
else { sigma = sigma_b;}

y[j] ~ normal(ipred[j], sigma); 

}
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In my data set, I have a covariate "flag_g" with the values of 0 and 1. Once "flag_g == 0", I want to use sigma_m as the residual error in the normal distribution. Once "flag_g==1", I want to use sigma_b in the normal distribution. Once I coded as above, I got rather insane result for both sigma_m, sigma_b and other fitted parameters. 

The thing made me wonder is once I didn't separate sigma_m and sigma_b as below, the fitted result was correct.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
model {   .....

   ipred[j] = (1-flag_g)*(function_1) + flag_g*(function_2);

y[j] ~ normal(ipred[j], sigma); 

}
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Could anyone suggest what was wrong with my code and how to do it right? Thanks a lot in advance!

Best Regards, Zheng

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How to code two different residual errors in Stan
parts:
Hi Zheng,

It's really hard to decipher what you're doing with just snippets like that.

At the very least, please provide the declarations of ipred, flag_g, function1, function2, and y. But really, it's better if you include the whole program.

If flag_g is an int, you might want to just to use an if statement. If the two sigmas you have are parameters, perhaps adding a prior would fix it?


Daniel

Hi all and Daniel,

Sorry this is my first time to ask question here in this usergroup. Maybe I didn't put myself very clear. I attached my stan code and R code as well as a portion of data set in this email. 
In fact I found something strange. If I wrote my code as below (please see the full code in the attachment), sigma_m and sigma_b worked fine. BUT I can fit correctly for only 9 subjects (ID=1~9). Strangely once I add the 10th subjects (all together then I have 10 subjects), the fitted result I got was insane. I can't figure out what went wrong. So your suggestions are really appreciated!

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
model {   .....

y[j] ~ normal(ipred[j], (1-flag_g)*sigma_m + flag_g*sigma_b);

}
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Best regards, Zheng

P.S. If you wish to test, please try to fit the whole data set first (with 10 subjects), but the result will be insane. Then please remove the subject ID=10, the fitting will go quite well with good results. Thanks a lot!
